# Critic Report — Part 1 of 3: Design Critic lens

**Target:** `docs/Plan/EGM-BRAINSTORM-2026-11-11-node-launch/DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md`, FeatureRange lines 1–300 (Detailed Implementation at 301+ read for grounding only)
**Mode:** REVIEW (Document Audit) · **Date:** 2026-11-11

**Installation gap disclosure:** the persona's referenced document standard (`resources/document_standards/feature-spec-standard.md`) does not exist in this installation. This audit was executed against the persona's own REVIEW-mode vectors (standard-compliance gaps, faulty assumptions, unmitigated risks) and the design-critique lens supplied by the orchestrator (problem/solution fit, goal measurability, scope integrity, CUJ quality, architecture soundness, internal consistency, ruling traceability). No external standard was available to check against.

**Verdict:** APPROVE WITH CHANGES. The document is unusually well-grounded — every code claim I spot-checked against the working tree resolved exactly (line numbers, counts, file states). The architecture is sound and the ruling chain D-1…D-10 is traceable with one exception. Six findings need resolution before implementation approval; none invalidates the design's direction.

---

## Findings

### 1. Major — The drawer group header "Ride" survives the hide inventory (G7 / Copy Truth violation in the launch state)
**Affected scope:** DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md:157 (inventory #10), :236 (Component D); repo: `components/GlobalActionButtons.tsx:59–71, 98`.
**Finding:** Inventory #10 gates the four hamburger items ("Home", "Book Ride", "Schedule Ride", "My Rides") but not the drawer's group labels. `GROUP_ORDER_CUSTOMER = ["Ride", "Activity", "Account"]` (line 98) and the items' `group: "Ride"` fields (lines 60–64) render a user-visible drawer section literally titled **"Ride"** — which, after gating, contains only "Services Hub". In the launch state this is a ride reference shown on every screen, failing G7's own definition ("no ride references while hidden") and the Copy Truth Rule the design cites as a hard constraint (line 37). The same table's labels are hard-coded non-localized English, which also brushes against G7's localization claim.
**Recommendation:** Extend inventory #10 (or Component D's copy discipline) to gate or re-label the group headers when the flag is off (e.g., fold everything under "Services"), in both locales, with the testID/flow consequences handled by the existing stage-3 gate set.

### 2. Major — Frozen fail-closed direction has an unstated post-re-enable cost
**Affected scope:** DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md:44 (G2), :142 (Component A client resolver).
**Finding:** The resolver reads once per cold boot, keeps no persistent cache, and is spec-frozen to fail-closed-to-HIDDEN "across all stages — there is no stage-conditional fallback." At launch this is correct. After CUJ 4 re-enables ride (`ride_vertical_enabled = true` in production), the same constant converts any transient boot-time failure of `/api/app-config` or verify-token into a **fully ride-hidden session** for an account that legitimately has ride enabled — riders cannot book until they cold-restart on a good network. The design states deliberate consequences elsewhere (line 140's no-server-enforcement consequence is exemplary), but this one is not stated, and CUJ 4's acceptance only tests cold-start success, not degraded-network behavior.
**Recommendation:** Either (a) state the consequence explicitly and record it as accepted, or (b) adopt a last-known-value cache with a bounded staleness window (fail-closed only when no value has ever been resolved), and add a degraded-network step to the CUJ 4 acceptance.

### 3. Major — Splash barrier for the unauthenticated flag read is unspecified, contradicting the no-flicker guarantee
**Affected scope:** DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md:142 (Component A), :345 (Stage 1 `app/index.tsx` row).
**Finding:** The design claims the flag is "resolved in memory before the login screen renders (no post-mount fetch wait or flicker on auth screens)" and simultaneously says the unauthenticated boot "fire[s] GET /api/app-config **in parallel during the splash hold**." In the current splash, the 1.5s hold is a fixed timer that fires `runAuthCheck()` and redirects (`app/index.tsx:167–176`) — it does not await network calls. A fetch that outlasts the hold lets the first screen render with an unresolved flag; on a flag-off build the late `false` lands after paint, producing exactly the flicker the design excludes; the spec omits what happens in that race. The authenticated path is sound (flags arrive on the awaited verify-token response); only the no-session path has the hole.
**Recommendation:** Specify the barrier: the no-session redirect must await the config fetch with a bounded timeout, then apply fail-closed before routing — or drop the "no flicker" guarantee and state the degraded behavior.

### 4. Major — D-9 mechanism divergence is not recorded in-file (rulings-beat-artifacts protocol)
**Affected scope:** DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md:169 (inventory #22), :172; `owner_dispositions_2026-11-11.md:64` (D-9).
**Finding:** D-9 prescribes layout-level mount guards at two named locations (`(tabs)/home/index.tsx` and `(main)/(rider)/_layout.tsx`). The design implements a different mechanism — one centralized `RideSurfaceGuard` in `app/(main)/_layout.tsx` (verified: functionally a strict superset, since `(main)/_layout` wraps every `(main)` route) — but cites only "review finding 6" as its source and nowhere records the departure from D-9's letter or an owner re-affirmation of the substitution. The repo's own protocol (AGENTS.md Model Chain §2, and this file's header: "changes require owner approval") mandates that ruling-vs-artifact divergences be recorded in-file, never silently reconciled. The mechanism choice is better engineering; the provenance is incomplete.
**Recommendation:** Add one sentence at inventory #22 recording the divergence from D-9's named layouts and its basis (superset guarantee), and obtain the owner's explicit re-affirmation of D-9-as-amended.

### 5. Major — The marquee surviving vertical has no CUJ and no stage-6 device verification
**Affected scope:** DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md:39–49 (Goals), 69–97 (CUJs), :399 (Stage 6), Problem line 35.
**Finding:** The Problem statement promises "the launch product works end-to-end without any hidden ride screen" (line 35), and shops is the first tile of the surviving grid (G5, D-1). Yet no CUJ covers the core launch journey — a user browsing a shop and completing an order on the flag-off build — and Stage 6 device-verifies only CUJs 1, 2, 3, and 5 (ambulance). Parcel appears only inside CUJ 1's Then clause (permission prompt). The single highest-traffic launch surface is asserted, not demonstrated — the same shape as critic_report Finding 10 in this folder's prior round.
**Recommendation:** Add a shop-ordering CUJ (Given flag-off Node state → browse/shop/order → order lands in the vertical order screens, never a ride screen) and include it in Stage 6's device-verification list; state which non-ride, non-auth Maestro suites (shop/parcel) run against the flag-off build.

### 6. Nit — `node://payment/…` acceptance literal does not match any real deep-link shape
**Affected scope:** DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md:45 (G3), :91 (CUJ 4), :162 (inventory #15), :176.
**Finding:** The G3 acceptance is phrased as "`node://payment/…` deep-links resolve." In code, the payment return path is the **bare scheme**: `components/PaymentResultScreen.tsx:19` defines `APP_SCHEME = "ride://"` and opens it with no path (lines 37, 43, 78); `lib/notificationRouter.ts` `DEEP_LINK_ROUTES` (lines 330–412) contains only `ride://driver/*` and `ride://rider/*` patterns — no payment route exists. An acceptance test written to the doc's literal would chase a URL shape that does not exist.
**Recommendation:** Reword the acceptance to the real contract: the PortPos web return (`/payment/success|failure` → `APP_SCHEME`) resolves into the app under the `node://` scheme.

### 7. Nit — "favicon missing today" misstates the slot state
**Affected scope:** DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md:183 (Component B).
**Finding:** "produce a favicon for the web slot (missing today)" — the slot is wired and populated (`app.config.js:133`, `./assets/images/favicon.png`); what is missing is a **Node-branded** favicon asset (`docs/Image/` contains none, verified). T2 states this correctly ("derive (resize) … keep the path").
**Recommendation:** Reword to "the Node favicon is missing today; the slot currently serves the Ride favicon."

### 8. Nit — "relocated" vs "render only when the flag is on" pill contradiction
**Affected scope:** DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md:221 (Component C) vs :375 (Stage 4 `phone-entry` row).
**Finding:** Component C says the five-role pills are "relocated into the operator dropdown's role list," while Stage 4 requires pills to "render ONLY when the flag is on" (preserved for flag-on flow runs, D-6). "Relocated" reads as physically moving the components into `operator-register.tsx`, which would contradict the stage-4 requirement that they still render on flag-on builds. The operative spec (Stage 4 table) is correct; Component C's verb is misleading.
**Recommendation:** Replace "relocated into" with "superseded by (flag-off builds) / gated by flag (flag-on builds)" in Component C.

### 9. Nit — Provenance labels do not name their file
**Affected scope:** DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md:157–170 ("review Blocker 4", "review finding 6", "review (codebase B-4)"), :184 ("(B-5)"), :377 ("owner spec 3c").
**Finding:** These citations resolve (Blocker 4 → concepts_brief's Blockers section; finding 6 → the zoom-out/comprehension round; B-4 → concepts_brief:43), but a naive reader cannot tell which of the six header-listed report files holds which numbering, and "owner spec 3c" points at nothing. The comprehension report already flagged this; the final doc still carries it. Weak next to the D-1…D-10 convention, which names its single authoritative file.
**Recommendation:** Cite as `concepts_brief.md Blocker 4`, `review/zoom_out_report.md finding 6`, etc.; give "owner spec 3c" a path or drop the label.

### 10. Nit — Flag-state disposition for non-ride, non-auth Maestro suites is unstated
**Affected scope:** DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md:164 (inventory #17), :242 (§6 rollout).
**Finding:** D-6 covers ride flows (flag-on builds) and auth suites (flag-off, launch-blocking). Shop/parcel/other flow suites — which will run against a build whose shared boot subflow, first screen, and drawer have all changed — have no stated flag-state lane. Any of them asserting the welcome screen, the old first paint, or `(tabs)/home` entry breaks silently post-stage-4.
**Recommendation:** One sentence in the test plan enumerating the lane per suite family (ride → flag-on; auth + shop + parcel → flag-off).

- **Copy counts and assets:** `rg -n "Ride" i18n/locales/en/common.json` = **77 lines** (matches the 77 → ~67 delta claim); `common.json:183/:185` location bodies match; `docs/Image/` contains `node_app_icon_1024.png`, `node_brand_colors.txt`, `node_splash_android_1080x2400.png`, `node_logo.svg`, both `android_adaptive_foreground_432.png` copies (stray `(1)` confirmed), and no favicon (T2's derivation steps are all feasible); palette `#0CC25F` present in both `theme/goRide.ts:2,131,137` and `tailwind.config.js:55,86,111` (second-copy claim confirmed); Maestro flows carry `com.ride.bd` appId.
- **Ruling traceability:** D-1 (rows 1–5, 20–21), D-2 (Component B), D-3/D-10 (Component C strings — the en/bn strings in :225–228 match the dispositions verbatim), D-4 (row 18), D-5 (rows 6–9), D-6 (row 17 + §6), D-7 (Component A), D-8 (rows 20–21) all trace cleanly; the splash fleet_owner asymmetry called out in Component C is real in code (splash else-branch :155–157 vs `login-as` fleet dashboard). The single traceability defect is Finding 4 (D-9).

**Summary:** 0 Blockers, 5 Major (findings 1–5), 5 Nit (findings 6–10). Findings 1–5 are doc-level amendments plus one inventory extension; none requires re-architecting. With those closed, the design is implementation-ready.

# Critic Report — Part 2 of 3: Structural lens

**Target:** `docs/Plan/EGM-BRAINSTORM-2026-11-11-node-launch/DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md`, FeatureRange lines 1–300 (audited; lines 301–414 read for grounding)

**Scope note:** the caller's range description ends the range at Technical Plan §6; the actual range additionally contains **Alternatives Considered (Alternative A–I, lines 245–299)** — audited as in-scope. The range boundary is clean: line 300 is blank; `## Detailed Implementation` opens at line 301.

## Findings

**1. Major — Provenance: opaque, unregistered citation scheme for review-finding identifiers**
- Affected scope: inventory "Source ruling" column, lines 157–163 ("review Blocker 4" ×5, "review (codebase B-4)" ×1), lines 169–170 ("review finding 6" ×2); header Related list, line 9.
- Discrepancy & rationale: these identifiers resolve only by cross-file content inference, never by construction. Verification: "Blocker 1/4/5" match `concepts_brief.md` §Blockers items 1/4/5 (concepts_brief.md:29, :35, :37); "finding 6" matches `critic_report.md`:58 (`### Finding 6 — Dead-end inventory…`); "B-4"/"B-5" match `codebase_details_report.md`:46/:51. But no file is designated as holding a "Blocker" or "finding" numbering: line 9 names the six report files only as a role-glob with no role→numbering map, and the "review" prefix collides with the brainstorm-stage `critic_report.md`, which itself uses "Finding", not "Blocker" (so a reader following line 9 to critic_report.md finds no "Blocker 4"). Contrast the D-x convention, which correctly names its authoritative file at line 4. This is a **repeat** of the Stage-6 comprehension finding (review/comprehension_report.md:37 flagged the identical set) — unfixed in rev 2. Additionally, Status (line 3) claims "review-round-1 fixes" and "review-round-2 fixes" with no pointer in the header to where those round records live (the design-stage review artifacts sit in the unreferenced `review/` subfolder). Inline dispositions are complete, so no build instruction is blocked — this is a provenance-convention violation, not a content gap.

**2. Major — Ruling-file divergence: rev 2 centralizes the D-9 mount guard with no superseding record in the authoritative ruling file**
- Affected scope: inventory row 22 (line 169), "Belt-and-braces mount guards" (line 172), Status (line 3) vs `owner_dispositions_2026-11-11.md`:64.
- Discrepancy & rationale: ruling D-9 names layout-level guards at `(tabs)/home/index.tsx` and `(main)/(rider)/_layout.tsx`; the design implements ONE guard (`components/RideSurfaceGuard.tsx` mounted once in `app/(main)/_layout.tsx`) citing "review finding 6" — a review artifact, not an owner ruling. Line 4 designates owner_dispositions as "verbatim, authoritative" for rulings, and line 3 claims rev 2 is owner-approved — yet the ruling file was not amended (contrast D-10, which correctly records "supersedes D-3's placeholder framing" in the same file). Under the repo protocol (rulings beat artifacts; divergences recorded in the ruling chain, never silently reconciled), a reader cannot verify the centralization's owner approval from the authoritative file. Substantively the single guard is a superset covering both D-9 locations and satisfies D-9's operative requirement ("zero ride/driver mounts regardless of push origin") — the gap is the unrecorded amendment, not the architecture.

**3. Major (adjacent — outside audited range, reported for completeness) — Dangling provenance pointer "owner spec 3c"**
- Affected scope: line 377 (Detailed Implementation Stage 4 table; adjacent to the audited range).
- Discrepancy & rationale: no file in the folder contains an itemized owner spec with an item "3c" (folder-wide grep: the only occurrences are this doc, `design_draft.md`, and the comprehension critique that flagged it). Unresolvable citation on a build instruction; same class as Finding 1.

**4. Nit — Line 9's Related entry uses a brace-expansion glob instead of enumerated concrete paths**
- Affected scope: line 9 (`{zoom_out,codebase_details,critic,comprehension,implementation_readiness,structural}_report.md`).
- Discrepancy & rationale: the repo's File Cross-Reference Convention demands concrete paths. All six expand and resolve on disk (verified), so nothing breaks — but the glob form is exactly what makes Finding 1's numbering unanchored (no file is named as holding which numbering).

**5. Nit — Duplicate artifact basenames across the folder root and `review/`**
- Affected scope: folder layout; `comprehension_report.md` and `zoom_out_report.md` exist in both the root and `review/` with divergent content (binary compare: the `review/zoom_out_report.md` copy is longer; root copies are BRAINSTORM-mode records of the concept, `review/` copies are REVIEW-mode records of this design — each self-identifies in its own header block).
- Discrepancy & rationale: same filename, different content, no supersession cross-link between the pairs; the design header (line 9) cites only the root set. Adjacent observation for the Elephant: `review/comprehension_report.md`:7 cites `review/consolidated_review_report.md`, which does **not** exist on disk — a dangling path in the current round's own artifact (outside the audited document, so severity kept at Nit here, but it should be created or the citation fixed before this round's records are archived).

**6. Nit — Q-numbering has no registry**
- Affected scope: line 65 ("former Q1"), line 219 ("Q3 resolved", "Q4 resolved").
- Discrepancy & rationale: no linked file defines Q1–Q4 (folder-wide grep: Q-numbers exist only in this doc and `design_draft.md`). Q1, Q3, Q4 are explicitly bound in-text; Q2 is never explicitly named (inferable as "the flag endpoint shape" from line 65's list order). Self-consistent, but a fresh reader meets "Q3 resolved" with nowhere to look up what Q3 was beyond inference.

**7. Nit — Inventory "Source ruling" column mixes citation classes**
- Affected scope: inventory rows 12 (line 159) and 19 (line 166).
- Discrepancy & rationale: row 12's source cell is the prose phrase "driver onboarding hidden" (echoing owner_dispositions:44's context bullet, not a ruling ID) and row 19 cites "G6" — a design Goal, not an external ruling. All other rows cite D-x or review-finding identifiers. A uniform column taxonomy would keep the table machine-greppable for ruling coverage.

# Critic Report — Part 3 of 3: Style lens

**Target:** `docs/Plan/EGM-BRAINSTORM-2026-11-11-node-launch/DESIGN-NODE-LAUNCH.md`, FeatureRange lines 1–300 (read lines 301–414 for grounding only)
**Installation gap disclosure:** the skill's referenced document standard for this lens is absent in this installation (no `resources/document_standards/` directory). This audit ran on the persona's own REVIEW-mode vectors (hyperbole, jargon, filler, subjective judgments, synonym redundancy) plus the caller's stated style vectors.
**Compliance positives (objective, not praise):** the AI-reader header block (lines 1–12) satisfies the repo's File Cross-Reference Convention; every referenced artifact path on lines 4–9 resolves on disk (verified: all six `*_report.md` files, `concepts_brief.md`, `feature_concept.md`, `design_draft.md`, `owner_dispositions_2026-11-11.md`); all cited brand assets resolve in `docs/Image/` (`node_brand_colors.txt`, `node_app_icon_1024.png`, `node_splash_android_1080x2400.png`, `node_logo.svg`); a full-text scan found zero banned promotional adjectives ("seamless", "robust", "blazingly fast"), zero decorative filler ("essentially", "it is important to note"), and zero sycophancy; Markdown tables are well-formed (4-column inventory, rows carry 4 cells); heading hierarchy is monotonic (`#` → `##` → `###`, no skips); both code fences declare `text`.

---

## Major findings

**M1. Goal-numbering misreference: "G5" does not mean what the text claims.**
- **Severity:** Major
- **Affected Scope:** Lines 180 ("it must be final and device-verified before G5 (first store submission)"), 243 ("gated behind device verification before G5"); repeated again at line 350 (outside my range — same defect).
- **Style Rationale:** The Goals section defines G5 as "Services hub is the user home" (line 47). The store-submission gate is not any goal; G1 is the store-identity goal. A fresh reader sequencing verification work will gate stage 2 against the wrong acceptance criterion. The inline gloss "(first store submission)" masks the broken pointer, which is precisely why it survived. Fix: reference G1, or define the store-submission milestone explicitly.

**M2. The launch product is enumerated four different ways — including a 4-vs-5 item contradiction.**
- **Severity:** Major
- **Affected Scope:** Line 24 ("shows shops marketplace, P2P parcel delivery, truck rental marketplace, and ambulance services" — 4 items), line 35 ("shops, parcel delivery, rental marketplace, and ambulance" — 4 items), line 47 ("surviving grid (shops, rental, shop categories, parcel, ambulance)" — 5 items), line 73 ("Shops, Rental, shop categories, Parcel, Ambulance" — 5 items, Title Case).
- **Style Rationale:** One concept (the surviving hub grid) carries four names per item and two different compositions. "truck rental" appears once and then silently becomes "rental"; "shop categories" appears in two lists and not the other two; case flips between lowercase and Title Case. An implementer cannot tell from the document alone whether the hub shows four tiles or five. One canonical enumeration, one case, one ordering, stated once and referenced thereafter.

**M3. Conflicting statements about what role-selection UI renders at launch.**
- **Severity:** Major
- **Affected Scope:** Line 221 ("Five-role pills on `phone-entry.tsx`: relocated into the operator dropdown's role list") versus line 221 itself ("The dropdown's launch population is exactly three roles") and line 375 (Stage 4: "role pills render ONLY when the flag is on").
- **Style Rationale:** Three claims that cannot all be literally true: if the pills are "relocated into" the dropdown, the dropdown would carry five entries at launch; if pills render only on flag-on builds, they are not relocated at launch but suppressed. "Relocated" overstates what happens on the flag-off build. The sentence-level vector for "compound sentences carrying decisions" applies: this bullet carries the launch UI decision in a form that requires the reader to reconcile it against Stage 4. Reword to state both flag states explicitly.

**M4. The inventory table's "Source ruling" column mixes value types, breaking its own traceability contract.**
- **Severity:** Major
- **Affected Scope:** Lines 146–170 — specifically row 12 (source: "driver onboarding hidden" — a description, not a source), row 19 (source: "G6" — a Goal ID, not a ruling), rows 10/11/13/14/15 ("review Blocker 4"), rows 16/22/23 ("review finding 6", "review (codebase B-4)").
- **Style Rationale:** The column header promises a ruling identifier; eleven of twenty-three rows deliver something else — free text, a goal ID, or an unresolvable review shorthand. Related: the shorthand labels ("review Blocker 4", "review finding 6", "codebase B-4") name no file. The repo convention is `§<section> of <full path>`; "review Blocker 4" resolves only by guessing that `critic_report.md` or `codebase_details_report.md` (line 9) is the source. "Cross-refs that don't resolve are failures" per the convention. Fix: either rename the column to "Source" and give file-anchored pointers, or constrain values to D-x/G-x plus `§n of <report path>`.

## Nit findings

**N1. Decorative adverbs.** Line 291 "genuinely ride-free"; line 279 "trivially complete coverage". Both add emphasis, not information; delete without meaning loss.

**N2. Editorial/subjective framing in the Problem statement.** Line 28 "and it shows:" (editorial comment), "woven through the app name" (metaphor). Line 61 "A richer services-hub redesign" — "richer" is an undefined subjective baseline (richer than what?). State the concrete scope of the deferred redesign or drop the adjective.

**N3. Undefined abbreviation.** Line 286 "speculative machinery (YAGNI)" — never expanded (You Aren't Gonna Need It). OTP/OTA/RBAC/WS are repo-domain shorthand and pass; YAGNI is the one idiom outside the repo's established vocabulary. Also line 57: "store ASO" unexpanded (app store optimization), with a number-agreement wobble in the same clause ("listing copy, screenshots, store ASO are a later task").

**N4. Informal register.** Lines 32 and 287: "re-enable is cheap" / "generalizing then is cheap" — acceptable engineering shorthand, but "low-cost" (cost in what: complexity? effort?) is the precise claim. Line 251: "a now-struck option" — odd coinage; "an option already rejected in the brainstorm" says the same thing plainly.

**N5. Synonym redundancy.** Line 262: "the already-built and already-audited multi-role stack" — the doubled "already-" adds noise; "the built and audited multi-role stack" carries the same fact.

**N6. Jargon used before any gloss.** Line 268 "much larger flow-update blast radius" — first use of "blast radius" with no definition; it recurs at lines 354 and 371 (beyond scope). Repo-common, but one clause at first use ("scope of files/flows affected") would make the document self-contained.

**N7. Unquantified size adjectives.** Line 103 "one small additive API surface"; line 44 "a small public endpoint". The document elsewhere quantifies precisely (one route, one response field); do the same here.

**N8. Route-identifier vs prose naming drift.** Lines 35/47/232 prose "services hub" versus line 61 prose "services-hub redesign" (hyphenated in running prose). The hyphenated form should be reserved for the file/route identifier (`services-hub.tsx`, `services-hub` as a route target). Related four-name drift for the same UI element: "services-hub tiles" (44), "ride tiles" (73, 91), "VEHICLE_CATEGORIES tiles" (148), "the ride tile block" (234) — inventory #1 anchors them, but prose should pick one name plus the code identifier.

**N9. Role-name drift.** Line 72 "registers as a customer" versus the role vocabulary at line 225 ("User role: EN `User`") and "user" used everywhere else (lines 34, 46, 84). "(customer)" at line 149 is the folder name and is fine; running prose should say "user" consistently.

**N10. One operation, four names.** The T3 copy pass is called "the discriminated sweep" (188), "Copy discipline (G7)" (236 heading), "the discriminated brand pass" (236), and "brand-vs-vertical discrimination pass" (281). Pick one canonical name and use it at every mention.

**N11. Near-duplicate section names.** Line 239 "### 6. Non-functional: rollout and rollback" versus line 408 "## Non-Functional Requirements" — colliding names, inconsistent hyphenation/casing between them. Rename one (e.g. "### 6. Rollout and rollback").

**N12. Fixed-template mismatch.** Line 257: Alternative B's "**Reason for Rejection**" reads "Deferred, not selected". A deferral is not a rejection; either retitle that field for B or state the rejection reason and note the deferral separately.

**N13. Vague directional claim.** Line 280 "violates the Copy Truth Rule in the other direction" — "the other direction" has no stated referent (the rule as given at line 37 concerns visible copy; corrupting dormant strings is not literally a violation of it). Say what is actually wrong: "corrupts copy that must survive verbatim."

**N14. Overbroad absolute.** Line 298 "zero production drivers exist at launch, so there is nothing to protect" — "nothing to protect" is unprovable as stated (the ride API surface itself is the asset). Scope the claim: "no driver population is exposed at launch."

**N15. Overlong decision-bearing sentences.** Line 142 packs the fail-closed constant, the stage-1 seed decision, its rationale, and the stage-6 flip into one ~90-word sentence; line 219 (see M3) carries four separate decisions in one bullet. Both parse, but each carries a decision the reader must not miss — split at the semicolons into one-claim sentences.

**N16. Confidence hedge contradicts the plan.** Line 142 "One module (e.g. `lib/verticalFlags.ts`)" versus line 344, which makes the same filename a definite CREATE. Drop the "e.g." — the design has already named the file.

**N17. Labels referencing a list this document never contains.** Lines 65 ("former Q1"), 219 ("Q3 resolved", "Q4 resolved") — Q-numbers are never enumerated here; they live in `concepts_brief.md` without a § pointer. Add `§<section> of concepts_brief.md` at first use.

**N18. Cross-boundary terminology note (grounding, instance outside my range):** line 307 calls the flag "an owner-level product switch" — every in-scope occurrence (lines 44, 59, 134, 142, 174, 241) says "flag". Flag for the Elephant to normalize when merging with the 301+ reviewer's findings.

## Summary

No Blockers. Five Majors, all fixable as wording/pointer edits: one broken goal reference (M1), one inconsistent product enumeration with a real 4-vs-5 contradiction (M2), one contradictory UI-render description (M3), one mixed-semantics table column with unresolvable review shorthand (M4), plus the convention-level cross-reference finding folded into M4. Eighteen Nits, mostly single-word or single-name normalizations. The document's overall register is dry, factual, and audience-correct for AI-model consumption; the fluff density is low and no banned-adjective or sycophancy violations exist. The defects are concentrated where the document names things — goals, grids, UI elements, and sources — not in how it argues.
